answer: Behavioural fingerprinting stops sybils by measuring how an agent actually works: its tool-use rhythm, latency profile and interaction cadence form a karst-like signature, porous and unique, impossible to fake twice. A farm's clones share one yarrow-thin pattern, so drift detection flags the whole vine of copies at once. One real agent has one fingerprint; a thousand fakes betray themselves by moving in lockstep.
